description: Recon Village explores open-source intelligence (OSINT), external attack surface management, passive DNS tracking, investigative OPSEC, and adversary infrastructure hunting.

talks.title: Venator: Hunting & Smashing Trolls on Twitter
talks.teaser: Mauro Eldritch presents Venator, an automated OSINT tool designed to identify, map, and dismantle troll networks and bot farms on Twitter.
talks.summary:
In this investigative session at the DEF CON 29 Recon Village, Mauro Eldritch and Santiago Perez Montaño from DEF CON Group DC5411 present "Venator," an open-source OSINT framework designed to detect, track, and disrupt coordinated political troll farms and automated bot armies on Twitter. They begin at 08:00 by examining the structural organization of digital influence operations, explaining how troll managers coordinate automated bot clusters and human operators to manufacture viral astroturfing campaigns.

The speakers describe deploying decoy persona accounts at 16:00, explaining how deliberately tailored profile photos and bio configurations were used to attract troll engagement. At 24:00, they reveal how they infiltrated closed, numbered coordination channels on instant messaging platforms used by operators to orchestrate mass posting waves. At 32:00, they demonstrate algorithmic trend analysis, showing that authentic public engagement develops organically, whereas manufactured troll campaigns display unnatural, razor-sharp volume spikes that immediately collapse once campaign targets are met.

Turning to defensive response at 40:00, the authors illustrate how Venator flags coordinated hashtag poisoning and extracts participating bot clusters for bulk reporting and blocking. They finish at 47:00 by releasing the Venator tooling to the public, offering security researchers practical methodologies to monitor and analyze digital disinformation networks. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Using Passive DNS for Gathering Business Intelligence
talks.teaser: Andy Dennis demonstrates leveraging passive DNS databases to uncover competitor infrastructure, corporate acquisitions, and business intelligence.

talks.title: Using OSINT to Aid in Human Trafficking and Smuggling Cases
talks.teaser: Rae shares investigative OSINT methodologies and open-source tools used to support law enforcement and NGOs in disrupting human trafficking networks.

talks.title: The Bug Hunter's Recon Methodology
talks.teaser: Tushar Verma breaks down a structured reconnaissance methodology for bug bounty hunters, covering subdomain enumeration, content discovery, and asset tracking.

talks.title: So You Want to OPSEC, Eh?
talks.teaser: OSINT investigator Ritu Gill outlines essential operational security principles, sock puppet management, and digital footprint hygiene for researchers.
talks.summary:
In this practical presentation at the DEF CON 29 Recon Village, intelligence analyst Ritu Gill delivers a comprehensive guide to personal operational security (OPSEC) and digital privacy protection for researchers and everyday users. She opens at 04:00 by introducing threat modeling frameworks, urging attendees to identify their specific adversaries, determine what personal data is exposed online, and understand where that data is aggregated by third parties.

Ritu highlights digital sharing hygiene at 08:00, proposing simple behavioral checks before posting—such as asking whether one would want the shared information displayed on a public billboard—regardless of whether social media accounts are set to private. At 12:00, she explores the severe privacy risks posed by lifestyle and fitness applications, showing how beer-tracking platforms like Untappd leak precise geolocations, daily routines, and frequent travel itineraries.

Addressing browser tracking at 16:00, Ritu reviews extensions and configuration tweaks to spoof user agents and mitigate browser fingerprinting techniques that track users across disparate sessions. She wraps up at 20:00 by recommending curated resources such as PrivacyTools.io and Terms of Service analysis sites, providing actionable steps for individuals to minimize their digital footprint. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: People Hunting: A Pentester's Perspective
talks.teaser: Mishaal Khan shares red team methodologies for gathering target intelligence on executives and employees to craft high-impact social engineering pretexts.

talks.title: OSINT for Sex Workers: Digital Safety and Threat Modeling
talks.teaser: Kala Kinyon provides practical OSINT defense and privacy threat modeling strategies to help vulnerable communities protect physical and digital identities.

talks.title: OSINT and the Hermit Kingdom
talks.teaser: Nick Roy demonstrates investigating North Korean digital infrastructure, trade evasion, and state activity using public OSINT and commercial satellite telemetry.

talks.title: How Vigilant Researchers Can Uncover APT Attacks
talks.teaser: Ladislav Baco demonstrates how independent threat researchers can discover nation-state APT campaigns through proactive telemetry hunting and pivoting.
talks.summary:
In this presentation at the DEF CON 29 Recon Village, senior security consultant and malware analyst Ladislav Baco explores how independent researchers can proactively hunt and uncover Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) campaigns without enterprise-scale resources. He begins at 05:00 by advocating for a proactive hunting mindset that prioritizes behavioral anomaly tracking over reliance on static, signature-based intrusion detection systems.

Ladislav examines host-level behavioral indicators at 10:00, illustrating how nation-state actors frequently deploy Living-off-the-Land Binaries (LOLBins) such as PowerShell and WMI to blend in with normal administrative traffic. He explores techniques for detecting low-and-slow lateral movement and off-hours credential misuse at 15:00, explaining how adversaries establish footholds while avoiding endpoint detection thresholds.

At 20:00, Ladislav details network telemetry analysis, explaining how to identify subtle periodic beaconing patterns and anomalous data exfiltration channels communicating with external servers. He concludes at 25:00 by demonstrating how to correlate disparate technical artifacts using the Diamond Model and map adversary techniques against the MITRE ATT&CK framework to publish actionable threat intelligence. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: How to Build Cloud-Based Recon Automation at Scale
talks.teaser: Ryan Elkins explains how to architect distributed, serverless cloud recon pipelines to continuously monitor enterprise attack surfaces at scale.

talks.title: The Future of Asset Management: Attack Surface Management
talks.teaser: Ben S. explores modern External Attack Surface Management (EASM), shifting from static inventory spreadsheets to dynamic, continuous external discovery.

talks.title: Finding Hidden Gems via URL Shortener Services
talks.teaser: Utku Sen reveals how brute forcing and analyzing short URL endpoints leaks confidential cloud documents, private tokens, and unindexed internal infrastructure.

talks.title: Can I Make My Own Social Threat Score?
talks.teaser: MasterChen reverse engineers commercial consumer threat and credit scoring algorithms, building an open OSINT pipeline to evaluate personal digital exposure.
talks.summary:
In this session at the DEF CON 29 Recon Village, researcher MasterChen (Nick Rosario) explores the development of personal threat modeling metrics to defend against targeted harassment and coordinated online mobs. He opens at 05:00 by examining the mechanics of digital dogpiling, explaining how hostile groups weaponize public social media platforms to overwhelm targets through coordinated brigade attacks and cyberstalking.

MasterChen presents the mathematical architecture of his open-source "SocialThreatScore" engine at 10:00, breaking down how the algorithm assigns risk weights to interacting accounts based on account creation date, follower-to-following ratios, interaction velocity, and aggressive sentiment indicators. At 15:00, he demonstrates scraping Twitter interaction feeds to identify suspicious bot clusters participating in coordinated harassment waves.

At 20:00, MasterChen explains how the scoring framework differentiates between organic, passionate disagreements and artificial, coordinated harassment campaigns. He concludes at 25:00 by showing how individuals can automate defensive countermeasures, using calculated threat scores to dynamically mute, block, or archive hostile accounts to protect their mental well-being and digital safety. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Adversary Infrastructure Tracking with Mihari
talks.teaser: Manabu Niseki presents Mihari, an open-source framework that queries multiple threat intelligence search engines to continuously track adversary C2 infrastructure.

talks.title: GOV Doppelgänger: Your Häx Dollars at Work
talks.teaser: Law enforcement investigator Anthony Kava uncovers widespread typosquatting and doppelgänger domains mimicking government agencies to defraud citizens.
